title: How do I increase the upload limit of st.file_uploader on Streamlit Community Cloud?
text:
# How do I increase the upload limit of st.file_uploader on Streamlit Community Cloud?

## Overview

By default, files uploaded using [`st.file_uploader()`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader) are limited to 200MB. You can configure this using the `server.maxUploadSize` config option.

Streamlit provides [four different ways to set configuration options](/develop/concepts/configuration):

1. In a **global config file** at `~/.streamlit/config.toml` for macOS/Linux or `%userprofile%/.streamlit/config.toml` for Windows:
   ```toml
   [server]
   maxUploadSize = 200
   ```
2. In a **per-project config file** at `$CWD/.streamlit/config.toml`, where `$CWD` is the folder you're running Streamlit from.
3. Through `STREAMLIT_*` **environment variables**, such as:
   ```bash
   export STREAMLIT_SERVER_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE=200
   ```
4. As **flags on the command line** when running `streamlit run`:
   ```bash
   streamlit run your_script.py --server.maxUploadSize 200
   ```

Which of the four options should you choose for an app deployed to [Streamlit Community Cloud](/deploy/streamlit-community-cloud)? 🤔

## Solution

When deploying your app to Streamlit Community Cloud, you should **use option 1**. Namely, set the `maxUploadSize` config option in a global config file (`.streamlit/config.toml`) uploaded to your app's GitHub repo. 🎈

For example, to increase the upload limit to 400MB, upload a `.streamlit/config.toml` file containing the following lines to your app's GitHub repo:

```toml
[server]
maxUploadSize = 400
```

## Relevant resources

- [Streamlit drag and drop capping at 200MB, need workaround](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/streamlit-drag-and-drop-capping-at-200mb-need-workaround/19803/2)
- [File uploader widget API](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader)
- [How to set Streamlit configuration options](/develop/concepts/configuration)

title: Where does st.file_uploader store uploaded files and when do they get deleted?
text:
# Where does st.file_uploader store uploaded files and when do they get deleted?

When you upload a file using [`st.file_uploader`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader), the data are copied to the Streamlit backend via the browser, and contained in a BytesIO buffer in Python memory (i.e. RAM, not disk). The data will persist in RAM until the Streamlit app re-runs from top-to-bottom, which is on each widget interaction. If you need to save the data that was uploaded between runs, then you can [cache](/develop/concepts/architecture/caching) it so that Streamlit persists it across re-runs.

As files are stored in memory, they get deleted immediately as soon as they’re not needed anymore.

This means Streamlit removes a file from memory when:

- The user uploads another file, replacing the original one
- The user clears the file uploader
- The user closes the browser tab where they uploaded the file

Related forum posts:

- https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/streamlit-sharing-fileupload-where-does-it-go/9267
- https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/how-to-update-the-uploaded-file-using-file-uploader/13512/

title: Widget behavior
text:
# Understanding widget behavior

Widgets (like `st.button`, `st.selectbox`, and `st.text_input`) are at the heart of Streamlit apps. They are the interactive elements of Streamlit that pass information from your users into your Python code. Widgets are magical and often work how you want, but they can have surprising behavior in some situations. Understanding the different parts of a widget and the precise order in which events occur helps you achieve your desired results.

This guide covers advanced concepts about widgets. Generally, it begins with simpler concepts and increases in complexity. For most beginning users, these details won't be important to know right away. When you want to dynamically change widgets or preserve widget information between pages, these concepts will be important to understand. We recommend having a basic understanding of [Session State](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state) before reading this guide.

1. The actions of one user don't affect the widgets of any other user.
2. A widget command returns the widget's current value, which is a simple Python type. For example, `st.button` returns a Boolean value.
3. Widgets return their default values on their first call before a user interacts with them.
4. A widget's identity depends on the arguments passed to the widget command. If a key is provided, the key determines the widget's identity, with limited exceptions noted in each widget's `key` parameter description. If no key is provided, changing a widget's label, min value, max value, default value, placeholder text, or help text will cause it to reset.
5. By default, if you don't call a widget command in a script run, Streamlit will delete the widget's information—_including its key-value pair in Session State_. If you call the same widget command later, Streamlit treats it as a new widget. Set `persist_state="page"` or `persist_state="session"` with a `key` to keep the value when the widget isn't rendered.
6. By default, widgets are not stateful between pages. If you have two widgets with the same key on different pages, they will be treated as two different widgets. Use `persist_state="session"` to keep a widget's value when the user navigates away and back.

The last three points (widget identity and widget deletion) are the most relevant when dynamically changing widgets or working with multi-page applications. This is covered in detail later in this guide: [Statefulness of widgets](#statefulness-of-widgets) and [Widget life cycle](#widget-life-cycle).

**Key-based widget identity (v1.55.0)**

As of v1.55.0, all widgets support key-based identity. When a `key` is provided, the key is the primary determinant of the widget's identity, and changing other parameters (like `label`, `options`, or `default`) won't reset the widget. Some parameters that constrain valid values still affect identity for specific widgets, even when a key is provided. For example, changing `min_value` or `max_value` for `st.slider` will reset the widget because the current value could be invalidated. These exceptions are noted in each widget's `key` parameter description.

Key-based identity was progressively introduced from v1.50.0 through v1.55.0. If you're using an older version, check the [release notes](/develop/quick-reference/release-notes) to see which widgets support key-based identity in your version.

**Other notable changes:**

- **v1.46.0**: When navigating between pages, widget keys in `st.session_state` are deleted at the beginning of the new page's script run instead of the end.
- **v1.55.0**: Most widgets support a new `bind` parameter to sync widget values with URL query parameters. See [Binding widgets to query parameters](#binding-widgets-to-query-parameters).
- **v1.59.0**: Most widgets support a new `persist_state` parameter to keep a widget's value when it isn't rendered. See [Keep a widget's value with persist_state](#keep-a-widgets-value-with-persist_state).

## Anatomy of a widget

There are four parts to keep in mind when using widgets:

1. The frontend component as seen by the user.
2. The backend (Python) in-memory value.
3. The key-value pair in `st.session_state` that provides programmatic access to the widget's value.
4. The return value given by the widget's function.

### Widgets are session dependent

Widget states are dependent on a particular session (browser connection). The actions of one user do not affect the widgets of any other user. Furthermore, if a user opens up multiple tabs to access an app, each tab will be a unique session. Changing a widget in one tab will not affect the same widget in another tab.

### Widgets return simple Python data types

The value of a widget as seen through `st.session_state` and returned by the widget function are of simple Python types. For example, `st.button` returns a boolean value and will have the same boolean value saved in `st.session_state` if using a key. The first time a widget function is called (before a user interacts with it), it will return its default value. For example, `st.selectbox` returns the first option by default. Default values are configurable for all widgets with a few special exceptions like `st.button` and `st.file_uploader`.

### Callbacks let you react to widget changes

Most widgets accept an `on_change` callback parameter (or `on_click` for buttons). A callback is a Python function that Streamlit calls when the user interacts with the widget. You can optionally pass arguments to the callback through the `args` and `kwargs` parameters. Callbacks are covered in detail in [Order of operations](#order-of-operations).

If you don't want a widget to rerun your app, set `on_change="ignore"` instead of passing a callback. The widget still updates in the browser, and your app receives the new value on the next rerun triggered by something else, such as another widget interaction. If the widget is [bound to a query parameter](#binding-widgets-to-query-parameters), the URL updates right away. Every widget with an `on_change` parameter supports `"ignore"`.

### Keys help distinguish widgets and access their values

Widget keys serve three purposes:

1. Distinguishing two otherwise identical widgets.
2. Maintaining statefulness of the widget while changing its parameters.
3. Creating a means to access and manipulate the widget's value through `st.session_state`.

Additionally, for developer convenience, keys are repeated in the DOM as HTML attributes with a Streamlit-specific prefix, `st-key-`, to prevent conflicts. The exact prefix, attribute name, and placement within the widget's DOM subtree aren't guaranteed to be stable between versions.

#### Widget identity: Key-based vs parameter-based

Whenever possible, Streamlit updates widgets incrementally on the frontend instead of rebuilding them with each rerun. This means Streamlit assigns a widget identity to each widget from the arguments passed to the widget command.

Widget identity depends on whether a key is provided:

- **With a key**: The key is the primary determinant of the widget's identity. Other parameters like `label`, `default`, `placeholder`, and `help` can change without resetting the widget. However, some widgets have specific parameters that also affect identity because changing them could invalidate the current value. For example, changing `min_value`/`max_value` on `st.slider` or `selection_mode` on `st.pills` will reset the widget even with a key. Check the `key` parameter description of each widget to see its exceptions, if any.
- **Without a key**: A widget's parameters (label, options, min/max, default, placeholder, help text) determine the widget identity. Changing one of these parameters will reset the widget. Note that callback functions, callback args and kwargs, label visibility, and disabling a widget do not affect the widget identity.

In all cases, widget identities aren't preserved between pages. By default, widget values aren't preserved between pages either. Use `persist_state="session"` to keep a value across page switches. More information is provided below in [Statefulness of widgets](#statefulness-of-widgets).

#### Streamlit can't understand two identical widgets on the same page

If you have two widgets of the same type with the same arguments on the same page, you will get a `DuplicateWidgetID` error. In this case, assign unique keys to the two widgets.

The following example will cause a `DuplicateWidgetID` error.

```python
st.button("OK")
st.button("OK")
```

The following example correctly assigns unique keys to the two buttons to avoid the `DuplicateWidgetID` error.

```python
st.button("OK", key="privacy")
st.button("OK", key="terms")
```

## Order of operations

When a user interacts with a widget, the widget is updated and triggers a rerun in the following order:

1. The widget value in `st.session_state` is updated.
2. The callback function (if any) is executed.
3. The page reruns with the widget command returning its new value.

If the callback function displays anything on the screen, that content will appear above the rest of the page. A callback function runs as a _prefix_ to the script run. Consequently, that means anything written via a callback function will disappear as soon as the user performs their next action. Widget commands should generally not be called within a callback function.

If a callback function is passed any args or kwargs, those arguments will be established when the widget command is called, not later when the user interacts with the widget. In particular, if you want to use a widget's value in its own callback function, you can't pass that value to the callback function via the `args` parameter; you must assign a key to the widget and look up its value using `st.session_state` _within the callback function_.

### Using callback functions with forms

Using a callback function with a form requires understanding of this order of operations.

```python
import streamlit as st

if "attendance" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.attendance = set()

def take_attendance():
    if st.session_state.name in st.session_state.attendance:
        st.info(f"{st.session_state.name} has already been counted.")
    else:
        st.session_state.attendance.add(st.session_state.name)

with st.form(key="my_form"):
    st.text_input("Name", key="name")
    st.form_submit_button("I'm here!", on_click=take_attendance)
```

## Statefulness of widgets

As long as the widget identity remains the same and that widget is continuously rendered on the frontend, then it will be stateful and remember user input. To keep a value when the widget isn't rendered, use `persist_state` as described below.

### Changing a widget's identity will reset it

If any of the parameters that determine a widget's identity change, Streamlit will see it as a new widget and it will reset. Providing a key protects the widget from resets when most parameters change. The use of default values is particularly important in this case. If you use a key and change a widget's default value, there will be no change to the widget's state. If you don't use a key, changing a widget's default value will reset the widget to that default value.

In this example, we have two sliders where you can change the min, max, and default values. Try interacting with each slider to change its value then change the min or max setting to see what happens. Because `min_value` and `max_value` constrain valid values, changing them resets `st.slider` even with a key. However, if you change the default value, only the slider without a key will reset. The keyed slider will remain stateful.

```python
import streamlit as st

cols = st.columns([2, 1, 2])
minimum = cols[0].number_input("Minimum", 1, 3)
maximum = cols[2].number_input("Maximum", 8, 10, 10)
value = cols[1].number_input("Default", 4, 7, 5)

st.slider("No key", minimum, maximum, value)
st.slider("With a key", minimum, maximum, value, key="a")
```

### Retain statefulness when changing a widget's identity

Here is a solution for the above example that preserves the slider's value when the min and max change. The widget's initial value is set through Session State rather than the `value` parameter. When you are programmatically changing a widget, use Session State to maintain the widget's state to avoid unexpected behavior.

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("a", 5)

cols = st.columns(2)
minimum = cols[0].number_input("Min", 1, 5, key="min")
maximum = cols[1].number_input("Max", 6, 10, 10, key="max")

def update_value():
    st.session_state.a = min(st.session_state.a, maximum)
    st.session_state.a = max(st.session_state.a, minimum)

update_value()
st.slider("A", minimum, maximum, key="a")
```

The `update_value()` function ensures consistency between the widget parameters and value. By writing to `st.session_state.a`, the key-value pair is available for use by the "new" widget. Without this write, Streamlit would overwrite the key-value pair with the default value. The reason for this is explained in [Widget life cycle](#widget-life-cycle).

### Widgets do not persist when not continually rendered

By default, if a widget command for a specific widget instance isn't called during a script run, then none of its parts are retained, including its value in `st.session_state`. If a widget has a key and you navigate away from that widget, its key and associated value in `st.session_state` are deleted. Even temporarily hiding a widget causes it to reset when it reappears; Streamlit will treat it like a new widget.

To keep a widget's value when it isn't rendered, set `persist_state` and provide a `key`.

#### Keep a widget's value with persist_state

`persist_state` can be one of the following:

- `None` (default): The value is dropped when the widget isn't rendered.
- `"page"`: The value is preserved while the user stays on the page where the widget is defined, for example while the widget is conditionally hidden. The value is discarded on a page switch.
- `"session"`: The value is preserved for the entire session, including across page switches, so it returns when the user navigates back.

`persist_state` requires a `key`. It is available on most widgets that support `bind="query-params"`. It is not available on `st.tabs`, trigger-like widgets (`st.button`, `st.download_button`, `st.form_submit_button`), file and media inputs (`st.file_uploader`, `st.camera_input`, `st.audio_input`), `st.chat_input`, `st.data_editor`, or selections from `st.dataframe` and charts.

Use `"page"` when a widget is hidden on the same page:

```python
import streamlit as st

if st.toggle("Edit name"):
    st.text_input("Name", key="name", persist_state="page")
```

Use `"session"` when the value should survive a page switch:

```python
import streamlit as st

st.text_input("Name", key="name", persist_state="session")
```

If `bind="query-params"` is also set, `bind` takes precedence: the value is stored in the URL, so it persists across page switches regardless of the `persist_state` scope.

## Widget life cycle

When a widget command is called, Streamlit will check if it already has a widget with the same identity. Streamlit will reconnect if it thinks the widget already exists. Otherwise, it will make a new one.

As mentioned earlier, Streamlit determines a widget's identity differently based on if it has a key. The page name also factors into a widget's identity, where widget identites are not preserved between pages. On the other hand, callback functions, callback args and kwargs, label visibility, and disabling a widget never affect a widget's identity.

### Calling a widget command when the widget doesn't already exist

If your script rerun calls a widget command with a changed identity or calls a widget command that wasn't used on the last script run:

1. Streamlit will build the frontend and backend parts of the widget, using its default value.
2. If the widget has been assigned a key, Streamlit will check if that key already exists in Session State.
   a. If the key exists and **isn't** associated to a widget with a different identity, Streamlit will assign that key's value to the widget.
   b. If the key exists and is associated to a widget with a different identity, Streamlit will overwrite the key-value pair with the default value. This is why writing to Session State before the widget command is important when [retaining statefulness across identity changes](#retain-statefulness-when-changing-a-widgets-identity).
   c. If the key doesn't exist, Streamlit will create a new key-value pair with the default value.
3. If there are args or kwargs for a callback function, they are evaluated and saved in memory.
4. The widget value is then returned by the function.

For step 2, prior to v1.46.0, Streamlit would ignore the value in Session State if it came from an instance of the widget on another page. This is because a widget on another page necessarily has a different identity. As of v1.46.0, Streamlit deletes such values at the beginning of a script run on a new page, unless `persist_state="session"` keeps them.

### Calling a widget command when the widget already exists

When rerunning a script without changing a widget's identity:

1. Streamlit will connect to the existing frontend and backend parts.
2. If the widget has a key that was deleted from `st.session_state`, then Streamlit will recreate the key using the current frontend value. This is because deleting a key from Session State will not revert the widget to a default value.
3. The widget command will return the current value of the widget.

### Widget clean-up process

Streamlit cleans up widget data at the end of every script run and at the beginning of a script run on a new page.

When Streamlit gets to the end of a script run, it will delete the data for any widgets it has in memory that were not rendered on the screen, unless `persist_state` is set. Most importantly, that means Streamlit will delete all key-value pairs in `st.session_state` associated with a widget not currently on screen. When you switch pages, Streamlit will delete all data associated with widgets from the previous page, except values kept with `persist_state="session"`. Values kept with `persist_state="page"` are discarded on a page switch.

## Binding widgets to query parameters

As of v1.55.0, most widgets support a `bind` parameter that syncs the widget's value with a URL query parameter. This makes it easy to create shareable URLs that preserve widget state and allow users to bookmark specific app configurations.

### How binding works

To bind a widget to a query parameter, set `bind="query-params"` and provide a `key`. The key is used as the query parameter name in the URL.

```python
import streamlit as st

st.selectbox("Color", ["Red", "Green", "Blue"], key="color", bind="query-params")
```

When a user selects "Green", the URL updates to include `?color=Green`. If someone opens that URL, the selectbox initializes to "Green" instead of the default "Red".

### Behavior details

- **Default values keep URLs clean**: When a widget's value matches its default, the query parameter is removed from the URL.
- **Invalid values are ignored**: If the URL contains an invalid value for the widget, the value is ignored and removed from the URL.
- **Programmatic updates**: A bound query parameter can't be set or deleted through `st.query_params`. To programmatically change a bound widget's value, use `st.session_state`.
- **Range values**: Widgets that return a range, like range sliders, use repeated query parameters. For example, a slider with a range of 10 to 90 will produce a URL ending with `?price=10&price=90`.
- **Browser history**: When a user navigates with the browser's back or forward buttons, bound widgets restore their values from the URL. If a bound parameter is missing from the URL, the widget returns to its default value.
- **`persist_state`**: If `bind="query-params"` and `persist_state` are both set, `bind` takes precedence. The value is stored in the URL, so it persists across page switches regardless of the `persist_state` scope.

Trigger-like widgets (`st.button`, `st.download_button`, `st.chat_input`, `st.file_uploader`, `st.camera_input`, and `st.audio_input`) don't support binding because their values are transient.

As of v1.65.0, [`st.expander`](/develop/api-reference/layout/st.expander) and [`st.tabs`](/develop/api-reference/layout/st.tabs) also accept `bind="query-params"` with a `key`, so a shared URL can keep an expander open or a specific tab selected.

### Example: Filterable dashboard with a shareable URL

```python
import streamlit as st

category = st.selectbox(
    "Category",
    ["All", "Electronics", "Clothing", "Books"],
    key="category",
    bind="query-params",
)
price = st.slider(
    "Max price",
    0, 1000, 500,
    key="max_price",
    bind="query-params",
)

st.write(f"Showing {category} items under ${price}")
```

With this setup, a URL like `https://myapp.streamlit.app/?category=Electronics&max_price=200` initializes the app with "Electronics" selected and the price slider set to 200. Sharing this URL gives others the exact same view.

## Best practices and recommendations

### For multipage apps

**Primary recommendation:** Use common widgets in the entrypoint file with [`st.navigation`](/develop/api-reference/navigation/st.navigation) to bypass page identity issues entirely:

```python
# streamlit_app.py (entrypoint)
import streamlit as st

# Common widgets that persist across all pages
user_name = st.sidebar.text_input("Name", key="global_name")
user_role = st.sidebar.selectbox("Role", ["User", "Admin"], key="global_role")

# Navigation
page = st.navigation([
    st.Page("page1.py", title="Dashboard"),
    st.Page("page2.py", title="Settings"),
])
page.run()
```

**Secondary recommendation:** For widgets that must be on individual pages, set `persist_state="session"` and provide a `key`. See [Keep a widget's value with persist_state](#keep-a-widgets-value-with-persist_state) for more information.

### For parameter changes

- Use keys when you need widgets to maintain state despite parameter changes.
- If you need to change a parameter that affects a widget's identity, use Session State to maintain the widget's value, or use a callback to directly maintain a widget's state. For more information, see [Retain statefulness when changing a widget's identity](#retain-statefulness-when-changing-a-widgets-identity). `persist_state` does not prevent a reset when a widget's identity changes.
- To force a widget to reset, update its key, or update a parameter without using a key.

title: Widget updating for every second input when using session state
text:
# Widget updating for every second input when using session state

## Overview

You are using [session state](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state) to store page interactions in your app. When users interact with a widget in your app (e.g., click a button), you expect your app to update its widget states and reflect the new values. However, you notice that it doesn't. Instead, users have to interact with the widget twice (e.g., click a button twice) for the app to show the correct values. What do you do now? 🤔 Let's walk through the solution in the section below.

## Solution

When using session state to update widgets or values in your script, you need to use the unique key you assigned to the widget, **not** the variable that you assigned your widget to. In the example code block below, the unique _key_ assigned to the slider widget is `slider`, and the _variable_ the widget is assigned to is `slide_val`.

Let's see this in an example. Say you want a user to click a button that resets a slider.

To have the slider's value update on the button click, you need to use a [callback function](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state#use-callbacks-to-update-session-state) with the `on_click` parameter of [`st.button`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.button):

```python
# the callback function for the button will add 1 to the
# slider value up to 10
def plus_one():
    if st.session_state["slider"] < 10:
        st.session_state.slider += 1
    else:
        pass
    return

# when creating the button, assign the name of your callback
# function to the on_click parameter
add_one = st.button("Add one to the slider", on_click=plus_one, key="add_one")

# create the slider
slide_val = st.slider("Pick a number", 0, 10, key="slider")
```

## Relevant resources

- [Caching Sqlite DB connection resulting in glitchy rendering of the page](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/caching-sqlite-db-connection-resulting-in-glitchy-rendering-of-the-page/19017)
- [Select all checkbox that is linked to selectbox of options](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/select-all-checkbox-that-is-linked-to-selectbox-of-options/18521)

# Issue #11115: session_state not preserved when using st.switch_page

Public issue report. State at snapshot: open. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

I encountered an issue while trying to pass data via session_state between the pages in my multi-page app using `st.switch_page`.

my_repository/
├── streamlit_app.py
├── page_1.py
├── page_2.py

`session_state.unit` is initialized through a checkbox in streamlit_app.py.
`session_state.unit` is lost upon clicking `st.switch_page` on page 2.
Interestingly, `session_state.unit` is preserved when navigating pages via the sidebar or using `st.page_link` on page 1.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
>>>>> streamlit_app.py <<<<<<<

import streamlit as st

st.sidebar.checkbox("set unit to True", key="unit")

pages = {
    "Your app": [
        st.Page("page_1.py", title="Page 1"),
        st.Page("page_2.py", title="Page 2"),
    ],
}
pg = st.navigation(pages)
pg.run()

>>>>> page_1.py <<<<<<<
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.unit
st.page_link("page_2.py", label="page_2") # this preserves state

>>>>> page_2.py <<<<<<<
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.unit
back = st.button("< Back to Page 1", type="primary")
if back:
    st.switch_page("page_1.py") # this causes state to be lost

### Steps To Reproduce

`session_state.unit` should be preserved after clicking `st.switch_page`

Public issue report. State at snapshot: closed. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

When uploading files with Unicode characters in their filenames (e.g., Hebrew, Arabic, Chinese, Emoji) using st.file_uploader on Streamlit Community Cloud, the upload fails with a 400 Bad Request error. The same code works without issue locally.

### Reproducible Code Example

import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Upload a file")
if uploaded_file is not None:
    st.write("File uploaded successfully.")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

מסמך.pdf (Hebrew)

اختبار.pdf (Arabic)

测试.pdf (Chinese)

テスト.pdf (Japanese)

file_🙂.pdf (Emoji)

"AxiosError: Request failed with status code 400"

Files should upload successfully regardless of the filename's character encoding.

I have noticed a small bug with `st.file_uploader` : regardless of whether `disabled` is `True` or `False`, it is always possible to remove files in the GUI.

import streamlit as st

st.session_state["disable"] = st.session_state.get("disable", False)

# Issue #12607: After File Upload the file stays in RAM

Public issue report. State at snapshot: closed. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

Watch discuss Topic:
https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/after-upload-file-stays-in-ram/119453/2

Streamlit Version 1.49.1
Python Version 3.13.7

I searched for the issue on all known databases without success

I am facing the following issue with st.file_uploader:

When I am uploading a File about 600MB the RAM usage is after I selected the File about 660 MB.
At the moment I pressed the upload button the RAM usage increases up to 1800MB.
After the Upload is done, the RAM usage stays at 660MB.
If I close the browsertab it stays at 660MB, only when I close the streamlit instance the RAM gets free.

I tryed several solutions:

clear_on_submit=True
working with session state keys
gc.collect()
st.rerun()

The phenomenon is:
If I set the clear_on_submit=false and deactivate the st.rerun() I am able to delete the File in the Widget and only then the file gets deleted from the RAM.

I tested it with a simple Upload code with the same result in different browsers on 2 different PCs and different streamlit versions.

Actually I have no idea how to fix this, can somebody help?

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
-------- Upload-Helper --------

def save_uploaded_file(file, folder):
os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
save_path = os.path.join(folder, file.name)

with open(save_path, "wb") as f:
    shutil.copyfileobj(file, f)

return save_path
def unified_upload(device_id):
st.subheader(“:open_file_folder: Dokument hochladen”)

# Dokumenttypen + erlaubte Dateiendungen
doc_types = {
    "Firmware": {"label": "💾 Firmware", "allowed_types": ["zip", "pdf"]},
    "Manual": {"label": "📘 Servicemanual", "allowed_types": ["pdf"]},
    "Partslist": {"label": "🛠️ Partslist", "allowed_types": ["pdf"]},
    "Bulletin": {"label": "📑 Bulletin", "allowed_types": ["pdf"]},
}

# Upload-Counter initialisieren
if "upload_counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.upload_counter = {}

if device_id not in st.session_state.upload_counter:
    st.session_state.upload_counter[device_id] = 0

# Dropdown zur Auswahl des Dokumententyps
doc_choice = st.selectbox(
    "Dokumenttyp auswählen",
    options=list(doc_types.keys()),
    format_func=lambda x: doc_types[x]["label"],
    index=None,
    placeholder="Bitte auswählen...",
    key=f"doc_select_{device_id}"
)

if not doc_choice:
    st.info("Bitte zuerst den Dokumenttyp auswählen ⬆️")
    return

# Zielordner für Gerät & Typ
folder = os.path.join(r"D:\ServiceInfoToolData", str(device_id), doc_choice)
os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)

# Dynamischen Key für file_uploader
file_key = f"file_upload_{device_id}_{doc_choice}_{st.session_state.upload_counter[device_id]}"

# Upload-Formular mit Auto-Reset
with st.form(f"upload_form_{device_id}_{doc_choice}", clear_on_submit=True):
    file = st.file_uploader(
        f"{doc_types[doc_choice]['label']} hochladen",
        type=doc_types[doc_choice]["allowed_types"],
        key=file_key
    )

    title = st.text_input("Titel (optional)")
    submitted = st.form_submit_button("Speichern")

    if submitted:
        if file is None:
            st.error("Bitte eine Datei auswählen.")
        else:
            save_path = save_uploaded_file(file, folder)

            # DB-Eintrag speichern
            conn = get_connection()
            try:
                conn.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO serviceinfos 
                    (geraet_id, typ, dateiname, pfad, uploaded_at, version) 
                    VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)
                    """,
                    (
                        device_id,
                        doc_choice,
                        file.name,
                        save_path,
                        datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                        title.strip() or None,
                    ),
                )
                conn.commit()
            finally:
                conn.close()

            # Upload-Counter hochzählen, damit nächster Upload einen neuen Key bekommt
            st.session_state.upload_counter[device_id] += 1

            # Speicher freigeben
            del file
            st.session_state._uploaded_file_mgr = UploadedFileManager()
            gc.collect()
            st.rerun()

            st.success(f"{doc_types[doc_choice]['label']} hochgeladen ✅")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use Upload Widget
2. activate clear on submit
3. upload larger file
4. watch in TaskManager the RAM behaviour

After Upload the RAM get free (file will be deleted from RAM)

### Current Behavior

RAM gets full

only if I deactivate the clear on submit and rerun I am able to delete the file via the x in the Widget after Upload and get the RAM free.

text:
# Issue #12800: libodbc2 conflicts with preinstalled libodbc1 from Microsoft in Streamlit Cloud

Public issue report. State at snapshot: closed. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

Trying to install `libodbc2` fails with the following message:

```
dpkg: error processing archive /tmp/apt-dpkg-install-NKXxq6/218-libodbc2_2.3.11-2+deb12u1_amd64.deb (--unpack):
 trying to overwrite '/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libodbc.so.2.0.0', which is also in package libodbc1:amd64 2.3.11-3
```

This shouldn't happen since `libodbc1` should be just a transitional package depending on `libodbc2`, but this specific version comes from the Microsoft repositories and doesn't do that.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set up a github repository with any trivial, "Hello world"-like streamlit app.
2.  Add a `packages.txt` and put just `libodbc2` in it.

title: Deleting a widget's session_state key leaves the frontend showing the stale value (backend/frontend divergence for one rerun)
text:
# Issue #16388: Deleting a widget's session_state key leaves the frontend showing the stale value (backend/frontend divergence for one rerun)

Public issue report. State at snapshot: open. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

Deleting a keyed widget's entry from `st.session_state` (e.g. `del st.session_state["foo"]` inside a callback) does not reset the widget, but can lead to an inconsistency between frontend and backend.

The Python side returns the widget's *default* value for that run, but the frontend keeps displaying the old value, so backend and frontend disagree.

On the **next** rerun the backend silently re-adopts the stale frontend value, so the deletion is effectively undone.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

text = st.text_input("Foo", value="default", key="foo")

st.write("widget returned:", repr(text))

def populate():
    st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"

def delete():
    del st.session_state["foo"]

st.button("Populate", on_click=populate)
st.button("Delete", on_click=delete)
st.button("Noop")

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app.
2. Click **Populate** (callback sets `st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"`). The text input now shows `hello` and `widget returned: 'hello'`.
3. Click **Delete** (callback runs `del st.session_state["foo"]`).
4. Observe the text input on screen vs. the `widget returned:` line.
5. Click **Noop** (any interaction that triggers a plain rerun) and observe again.

### Expected Behavior

The widget value in the frontent and backend should be consistent. After deleting a widget's key in session state, it should presumably fall back to its default value.

### Current Behavior

- After clicking Delete, the backend returns `widget returned: "default''` , but the frontend widget still displays `"hello"`.
- After the next rerun (step 5), the backend re-adopts the stale frontend value, and both show `"hello"`.

### Screenshot

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.2
- Python version: 3.14.6
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04

title: A config that sets server.port raises at config parse and blocks startup on a dev-mode (non-site-packages) install
text:
# Issue #17031: A config that sets server.port raises at config parse and blocks startup on a dev-mode (non-site-packages) install

Public issue report. State at snapshot: open. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

Setting `server.port` raises out of config parsing and blocks startup when Streamlit considers itself a development install, and the message does not say how to proceed.

`streamlit/config.py` defines `global.developmentMode` as true whenever the package is not under a `site-packages` directory (`"site-packages" not in __file__` — so a source checkout, `pip install -e`, or a vendored/`--target` install), and `_check_conflicts()` then raises:

```
RuntimeError: server.port does not work when global.developmentMode is true.
```

The raise looks deliberate — in dev mode the Node server hard-codes 8501, which is what the comment above the check explains — so this is a question about the *failure mode* rather than a claim that the check itself is wrong. Two things make it awkward from an application author's side:

1. **A committed config value is enough.** An app that ships `[server] port = ...` in its `.streamlit/config.toml` (a normal thing to pin for a deployment) cannot start *at all* on a dev-mode install, and the author may never have intended that value for this environment.
2. **The error does not name a way forward.** It says why the port does not work, not what to do about it. The escape hatch (below) is not discoverable from the message.

### Steps to reproduce

Self-contained; `pip install --target` is just a convenient way to get a non-`site-packages` install.

```bash
WORK=/tmp/streamlit-devmode-repro
python3 -m pip install --quiet --target "$WORK/pkgs" "streamlit==1.64.0"
mkdir -p "$WORK/app/.streamlit"
printf '[server]\nport = 9999\n' > "$WORK/app/.streamlit/config.toml"
cd "$WORK/app"

# 1. Any library use that parses config
PYTHONPATH="$WORK/pkgs" python3 -c "import streamlit.config as c; c.get_config_options()"
# RuntimeError: server.port does not work when global.developmentMode is true.

# 2. The CLI
PYTHONPATH="$WORK/pkgs" python3 -m streamlit config show
# same RuntimeError

# 3. Even with no port in any config file:
PYTHONPATH="$WORK/pkgs" python3 -m streamlit config show --server.port 8502
# same RuntimeError
```

All three exit 1. With a config that sets no port, the same install parses fine (`server.port` = 8501).

### Expected behavior

One of:

- warn and ignore the configured port (nothing needs it in dev mode, and the server uses 8501 regardless), or
- raise only for the port the server would actually use, and have the message name the escape hatch, e.g. *"remove `server.port` from `.streamlit/config.toml`, or run with `--global.developmentMode false`"*.

### Actual behavior

A hard `RuntimeError` from `get_config_options()`, before any app code runs, for any source of the value: a project or machine config file, or the documented `--server.port` flag.

### Is this new?

The same on 1.63.0 and 1.64.0 (in 1.63 the check sits at the end of `streamlit/config.py`, reached via `_on_config_parsed`). I have not checked further back.

### Workarounds (both verified)

- `streamlit run app.py --global.developmentMode false` — per run.
- `[global] developmentMode = false` in a config file — persistent, but it is a hidden option and it also turns off dev-mode conveniences (e.g. `logger.level` defaulting to `debug`).

### Environment

- Streamlit 1.63.0 and 1.64.0
- Python 3.13.14
- macOS 27.0 (arm64)

title: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value
text:
# Issue #17119: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value

Public issue report. State at snapshot: closed. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for that run. A follow-up rerun clears the printed backend as well.

Without the sibling edit, A→B→A can keep UI and backend aligned at `"input 2"`. Either interpretation of leftover keys should keep UI and printed state in sync; the #3512 unmount rule for an already-registered `persist_state=None` widget is that both sides reset in the same run.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current develop / #17106
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright)

### Additional Information

Found during QA of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17106#issuecomment-5813147965.

Related:

- #3512 — unmount should reset both the widget UI and the Python value in the same run
- #17093 / #17106 — delayed first mount after a leftover pre-registration user key (out of scope here)
- #12880 — identity-by-key (out of scope)

title: st.multiselect without key drops the user's selection when options come in a different order on rerun
text:
# Issue #17210: st.multiselect without key drops the user's selection when options come in a different order on rerun

Public issue report. State at snapshot: open. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

If `st.multiselect` has no `key` and its `options` list comes back in a different order on the next run, every selection the user makes is thrown away. The widget briefly shows the new chip, then flickers back to the default. Passing `sorted(options)` makes it work, and so does setting any `key`.

The order of options is often unstable in real apps: `list(set(...))`, `df[col].unique()` after a filter, SQL queries without `ORDER BY`, dict/set unions, and "move selected to top" patterns.

Similar reports were closed as expected behavior (#5995, #8496). #11277 fixed the case where `key` is set. The keyless case still resets, even though multiselect doesn't need it to.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import random
import streamlit as st

opts = ["apple", "banana", "cherry", "date", "elderberry"]
random.shuffle(opts)  # stands in for list(set(...)), an unordered query, etc.

sel = st.multiselect("Fruits", opts)  # works with sorted(opts) or key="fruits"
st.write(sel)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app.
2. Pick any option in the multiselect.

### Expected Behavior

The option stays selected, because the set of options didn't change and only their order did.

### Current Behavior

The chip appears for a moment and then disappears. `sel` is `[]`. Measured with `AppTest` on 1.64.0:

| options | key | value after select | value after next rerun |
|---|---|---|---|
| sorted | no | `['banana']` | `['banana']` |
| sorted | yes | `['banana']` | `['banana']` |
| shuffled | no | `[]` | `[]` |
| shuffled | yes | `['banana']` | `['banana']` |

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

Field | Value
-- | --
Streamlit version | 1.64.0
Python version | 3.12
Operating System | Linux
Browser | Chrome

### Additional Information

### Why this happens

In `lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/multiselect.py`, when there is no `key`, the widget ID is a hash of the widget parameters, including the **ordered** list of formatted options and the **indices** of the defaults:

```python
element_id = compute_and_register_element_id(
    widget_name,
    user_key=key,
    key_as_main_identity={"max_selections", "accept_new_options"},
    ...
    options=formatted_options,   # order-sensitive
    default=default_values,      # indices into options, also order-sensitive
    ...
)
```

With a new order, the ID changes on every run. When the user clicks, the frontend sends the value under the old ID. The rerun registers a widget with a new ID and no stored state, so it falls back to `default`. The frontend then mounts a new component with that ID, which is the flicker.

For multiselect, including the order isn't needed. The value travels as a list of **formatted option strings** (`string_array_value`), not indices. `MultiSelectSerde.deserialize` maps strings back with `formatted_options.index(v)`, and `validate_and_sync_multiselect_value_with_options` already handles options that change. The same selection means the same thing in any order.

### Proposed fix

Hash the options without regard to order, and hash defaults by value rather than by index:

```diff
             dg=self.dg,
             label=label,
-            options=formatted_options,
-            default=default_values,
+            # Values are stored as formatted strings rather than indices, so the
+            # order of options doesn't change their meaning. Hash options
+            # order-insensitively so reordering them doesn't reset the widget.
+            options=sorted(formatted_options),
+            default=[formatted_options[i] for i in default_values],
             help=help,
             max_selections=max_selections,
```

`proto.options` and `proto.default` are unchanged, so the display order still follows what the user passed. Only the identity hash changes. With this patch applied to 1.64.0, all four rows in the table above keep the selection, including with `default=[...]` set.

Notes:
- Existing keyless multiselects get new IDs once after upgrading. That's the same one-time reset any ID-scheme change causes.
- `selectbox`, `pills`, and `segmented_control` probably need the same change wherever they send values as strings. I haven't checked those.

title: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued
text:
# Issue #17215: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued

Public issue report. State at snapshot: closed. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

A Custom Components v2 (CCv2) `setTriggerValue` call is silently lost when its rerun request is still queued and another widget update arrives before the script runner picks it up: the `on__change` callback never runs and `result.` is never set. `st.button` survives the identical sequence. With default settings this affects components inside [redacted email]`, and with `runner.fastReruns = false` it also affects full-app reruns.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time

import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("log", [])

probe = st.components.v2.component(
    "trigger_probe",
    html="<button id='fire'>Fire component trigger</button>",
    js="""
export default function (component) {
  const { parentElement, setTriggerValue } = component;
  parentElement.querySelector("#fire").onclick = () => setTriggerValue("fired", Date.now());
}
""",
)

@st.fragment
def panel():
    # result.fired only exists for events with an on_<event>_change callback.
    result = probe(key="probe", on_fired_change=lambda: None)
    if result.fired:
        st.session_state.log.append("component trigger received")
    if st.button("st.button"):
        st.session_state.log.append("st.button click received")
    st.text_input("Other widget", key="other")
    st.write("Received:", st.session_state.log)
    time.sleep(5)  # a slow fragment, so the next requests queue up

panel()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run app.py` and wait for the first run to finish (about 5 s).
2. Click **Fire component trigger** while the app is idle. `Received:` shows `component trigger received`. This is the control.
3. Type `a` into **Other widget** and press Enter. The fragment reruns and sleeps for 5 s.
4. Within those 5 s, click **Fire component trigger**, then replace the text in **Other widget** with `b` and press Enter.
5. Wait for the fragment to finish.
6. Repeat steps 3–5, but click **st.button** instead of **Fire component trigger**.

### Expected Behavior

After step 5 the log gains a second `component trigger received`, the same way step 6 adds `st.button click received`.

### Current Behavior

After step 5 the log still holds only the control entry: the trigger fired in step 4 never reaches Python, although the text input's new value is applied. After step 6, `st.button click received` is appended as expected.

A full-app version of the script (the same body without [redacted email]`) behaves the same way when started with `--runner.fastReruns false`.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (also reproduced on 1.63.0)
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: macOS 27.0
- Browser: Chromium 152

### Additional Information

**Why it happens.** `AppSession.request_rerun` stops the current runner and starts a new one only when `runner.fastReruns` is on and the request has no `fragment_id`. A widget-triggered fragment rerun (or any rerun when `fastReruns` is off) is handed to the existing `ScriptRunner`. A fragment rerun also does not preempt the running script (`_fragment_run_should_not_preempt_script`), so it waits in the queue. If a rerun request is already queued, `ScriptRequests.request_rerun` merges the two requests with `_coalesce_widget_states(old, new)`. That keeps the newer message's widget states and carries forward only `trigger_value` and `chat_input_value` from the older one.

A CCv2 trigger is a `json_trigger_value` on the component's synthetic aggregator ID (`$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY___events`). The frontend deletes trigger values once it has sent them, so the newer message never contains the trigger, and the merge drops it.

`string_trigger_value`, used by `st.menu_button` and `st.column_config.ButtonColumn`, is missing from the same list. Checking `_coalesce_widget_states` directly on 1.64.0, with a queued trigger of each type followed by a newer message for another widget:

| Queued trigger type | Kept after the merge |
|---|---|
| `trigger_value` (`st.button`) | yes |
| `chat_input_value` (`st.chat_input`) | yes |
| `string_trigger_value` (`st.menu_button`, `ButtonColumn`) | no |
| `json_trigger_value` (CCv2 `setTriggerValue`) | no |

I reproduced the CCv2 case in the browser. The `string_trigger_value` row is from the function-level check only.

**Suggested fix.** 1.64.0 already has `_TRIGGER_PROTO_FIELDS` and `_has_active_trigger_value`, and `_coalesce_replay_trigger_states` uses them. `_coalesce_widget_states` could apply its existing carry-forward rule to every active trigger type through the same helper, instead of the hard-coded two-item list. When both messages carry a `json_trigger_value` for the same aggregator ID, concatenating the two event lists would keep both events. A rough sketch:

```python
import json  # not imported in script_requests.py today

def _trigger_events(state):
    events = json.loads(state.json_trigger_value)
    return events if isinstance(events, list) else [events]

# In _coalesce_widget_states, replacing the loop over the two-item list:
for old_state in old_states.widgets:
    if not _has_active_trigger_value(old_state):
        continue
    trigger_type = old_state.WhichOneof("value")
    new_state = states_by_id.get(old_state.id)
    if new_state is None or (
        new_state.WhichOneof("value") == trigger_type
        and not _has_active_trigger_value(new_state)
    ):
        # Today's rule, applied to every trigger type.
        states_by_id[old_state.id] = old_state
    elif trigger_type == "json_trigger_value" == new_state.WhichOneof("value"):
        # Both messages carry CCv2 events for one aggregator: keep both lists.
        merged = WidgetState()
        merged.CopyFrom(new_state)
        merged.json_trigger_value = json.dumps(_trigger_events(old_state) + _trigger_events(new_state))
        states_by_id[old_state.id] = merged
```

With this patched in at startup on 1.64.0, the browser repro above passes: the trigger fired in step 4 reaches Python, and the text input's new value is applied too. At the function level it keeps all four trigger types from the table and merges two events sent to one aggregator into a single list.

**Related.** The automated triage comment on #16732 (mount-time `setTriggerValue` dropped) noted this gap. The fix that closed it, #16833, made one non-test change, to `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive` in the frontend, so this backend path is unchanged. #16765 added the replay-trigger helpers that the fix above could reuse. The tech spec in the open spec PR #16763 (session-owned rerun mailbox) lists all four trigger types as ones that "may not be dropped by coalescing" and calls this the carry-forward already implemented. In 1.64.0, `_coalesce_widget_states` carries two of them. The same two-item list is on `develop` as of 2026-10-01 and in 1.52.0, so this is not a regression.

title: Enter to submit forms: submit instructions do not always show, even if Enter will submit the form
text:
# Issue #7079: Enter to submit forms: submit instructions do not always show, even if Enter will submit the form

Public issue report. State at snapshot: closed. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

With Streamlit 1.25.0 you can now Enter to submit a from from `st.text_input`, `st.text_area`, and `st.number_input`.

Submit instructions appear in those widgets mentioned above when a user makes a change to them. However, if a user leaves and returns to the widget without submitting the form, the submit instructions no longer appear. Nevertheless, Enter will still submit the form. This may be confusing and result in unintentional submissions.

Similarly, if a user makes no change to one any of the widgets in a form, the submit instructions do not appear when active in one of the widgets, but the form can still be submitted with Enter from such a widget.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

col1.write('')
col1.header('Outside a form')
outside_text = col1.text_input('Outside text input')
outside_area = col1.text_area('Outside text area')
col1.divider()

col1.subheader('Values from outside')
col1.write('Text input: ' + outside_text)
col1.write('Text area: ' + outside_area)

my_form = col2.form('my_form_key')
my_form.header('Inside a form')
inside_text = my_form.text_input('Inside text input')
inside_area = my_form.text_area('Inside text area')
my_form.form_submit_button('Submit form')

col2.subheader('Values from inside')
col2.write('Text input: ' + inside_text)
col2.write('Text area: ' + inside_area)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Change the value in a widget within the form
2. See submission instructions
3. Click out of the widget
4. Click back into the widget
5. See there are no submission instructions
6. Press enter (or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) and see that the form still submits

### Expected Behavior

Since the Enter-to-submit functionality is always active when active/focused in `st.text_input`, `st.text_area`, or `st.number_input` in a form, the submission instructions should always display when active/focused in those widgets within a form.

### Current Behavior

The Enter-to-submit instructions only display if you have edited that widget and haven't left the active/focus state for it. This is likely a carryover effect since widgets outside of forms will not trigger a rerun if submitted (Enter) when containing the same value as they had on the last rerun. Forms introduce a different pattern.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.25.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: MacOS
- Browser: FIrefox

### Additional Information

_No response_

# Issue #7216: Callback state change issue on date widget

Public issue report. State at snapshot: open. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

I tried searching for comparable issues using: ```is:issue is:open callback -label:type:enhancement``` but I could not find a direct match..

The issue I'm running into is that the callback function on the datepicker widget fires when the state is set programmatically _using `datetime`_. So pretty much all the input fields in the datepicker widget accept `datetime` and implicitly cast them to `date`. This is fine behavior and just works. But when setting the underlying state it gives a problem, when setting the underlying state to a date programmatically the callback does not fire. This is correct behavior in my opinion. The callback should only fire when actually using the input widget. But when setting the underlying state to a `datetime`, it's cast to a `date` _and_ the callback fires. I'm guessing it's caused by the cast?

### Reproducible Code Example

[](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7216)

```Python
import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st

def updated():
    if st.session_state.get("thingy"):
        st.write(st.session_state.thingy)
    st.write(dt.datetime.now())

def update_value():
    # Uncomment/comment the below lines to go from correct to incorrect behavior
    # st.session_state.thingy = st.session_state.thingy + dt.timedelta(days=1)
    st.session_state.thingy = dt.datetime.now()

def main():
    st.title("reproducible")
    st.date_input("thingy", key="thingy", on_change=updated)
    st.button("update thingy", on_click=update_value)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Click the button. The callback fires even though the user does not click the datepicker.

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the callback not to fire when setting it's state programmatically.. This is indeed the behaviour when setting the state to a `date` but when setting it to a `datetime` the callback fires.

text:
# Issue #8534: Unable to upload >980 files using file_uploader

Public issue report. State at snapshot: open. This is a report, not official diagnosis or proof of a fix.

### Summary

We have an application where we process a set of files, sometimes more than 2000.
The file_uploader widget hangs, then eventually produces a network error when the number of images exceeds 980.

This issue wasn't previously occurring. We did run into one issue where we had to increase the Python recursion limit since we iterate over each file and the default Python recursion limit is 1000 (I assumed ~20 or so iterations went to setup/config), and would produce an error. So we set the recursion limit to the number of files uploaded + 50.

Now, the `file_uploader` widget fails to upload >980 files. 980 works fine, and 981 uploads all but one. I looked at the source code and didn't see any upper limit defined for this operation. Logs don't show anything besides hanging until there are exactly 980 files, at which point it returns the list of uploaded files and continues executing the script.

Wondering if internally the recursion limit is being met, and might need to be increased.
Otherwise, please help us determine why we are now running into this issue. We were previously using streamlit version 1.29.0, and upgraded to 1.33.0 to find the issue still persists.

Thank you!

# 2026 release notes

This page contains release notes for Streamlit versions released in 2026. For the latest version of Streamlit, see [Release notes](/develop/quick-reference/release-notes).

## **Version 1.66.0**

_Release date: October 14, 2026_

**Highlights**

- 📐 Introducing the `theme.paddingTop` and `theme.paddingBottom` [config options](/develop/api-reference/configuration/config.toml#theme), so you can set the space between the app chrome and your page content, with optional `[theme.sidebar]` overrides ([#17350](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17350), [#6336](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6336)).
- 🎛 Announcing `on_change="ignore"` for every stateful widget, so a new value updates the widget and any bound query parameter without a rerun, and Python receives it on the next rerun ([#5827](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5827)). This release adds the remaining widgets:
    - [`st.pills`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.pills) and [`st.segmented_control`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.segmented_control) ([#17307](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17307), [#17452](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17452)).
    - [`st.feedback`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.feedback) ([#17281](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17281)).
    - [`st.color_picker`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.color_picker) ([#17209](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17209)).
    - [`st.datetime_input`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.datetime_input) ([#17267](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17267)).
    - [`st.camera_input`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.camera_input) and [`st.audio_input`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.audio_input) ([#17246](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17246), [#17328](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17328)).
    - [`st.data_editor`](/develop/api-reference/data/st.data_editor) ([#17347](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17347)).
    - [`st.pagination`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.pagination) ([#17397](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17397)).

**Notable Changes**

- 🧭 Apps have a "Skip to main content" link and `` and `` landmarks for keyboard and screen-reader users. Custom CSS selectors like `section[data-testid="stMain"]` should drop the tag ([#17418](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17418), [#17338](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17338), [#17416](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17416)).
- 🧪 [`AppTest`](/develop/api-reference/app-testing/st.testing.v1.AppTest) supports more elements:
    - `at.form` and `at.form_submit_button` let you look up forms by key and click their submit buttons ([#17229](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17229)).
    - `at.link_button` and `at.page_link` ([#17308](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17308)).
    - `at.progress`, `at.html`, and `at.help` ([#17280](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17280)).
    - `at.pagination` can select a page for the next run ([#17322](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17322)).
    - `at.audio_input` and `at.camera_input` can stage a recording or photo for the next run ([#17346](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17346), [#17459](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17459)).
- 🐍 Streamlit supports Python 3.15 ([#17426](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17426), [#17422](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17422)).
- 👻 Due to end of life, Python 3.10 is no longer supported. The minimum supported versions of NumPy, pandas, Pillow, and PyArrow are raised to releases with Python 3.11 wheels ([#17315](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17315)).

**Other Changes**

- 📦 `httptools` is now an optional dependency. Install `streamlit[performance]` to keep Uvicorn's faster HTTP parser ([#16554](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16554)).
- 💿 Streamlit no longer requires the `toml` dependency ([#17315](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17315), [#17342](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17342)).
- ⚠ Streamlit logs a startup warning when `websockets` 17 or later is installed with `uvicorn` older than 0.52.0, a combination that can break the WebSocket handshake behind proxies that forward non-ASCII headers ([#17115](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17115), [#16030](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16030)).
- 🐛 Bug fix: [`st.switch_page`](/develop/api-reference/navigation/st.switch_page) and [`st.page_link`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.page_link) reject Windows network and device paths before resolving them, so untrusted input can't trigger an SMB connection ([#17301](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17301)).
- 🦋 Bug fix: A disabled [`st.download_button`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.download_button) with a callable `data` argument no longer registers a download that can run the callable ([#17288](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17288)).
- 🪲 Bug fix: Apps embedded in an iframe sandboxed without `allow-same-origin` render instead of staying blank ([#17409](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17409), [#17402](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17402)).
- 🐜 Bug fix: A run that is stopped or replaced while waiting for another run's cached value exits promptly instead of holding a thread ([#17340](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17340)).
- 🐝 Bug fix: Streamlit logs an error at startup when `secrets.toml` can't be parsed, instead of silently continuing with empty secrets ([#17428](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17428)).
- 🐞 Bug fix: Checking for a missing `st.*` attribute with `hasattr` or `getattr` no longer imports modules, which could raise a `RuntimeError` in code that iterates `sys.modules` ([#17311](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17311), [#17298](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17298)).
- 🕷️ Bug fix: A fragment callback that only calls `st.switch_page` or `st.stop` no longer logs a false warning about displaying elements ([#17292](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17292)).
- 🪳 Bug fix: Keyed containers no longer trigger React key warnings or remount while a rerun is in progress ([#17456](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17456)).
- 🪰 Bug fix: Side-by-side elements line up better: `height="stretch"` elements in horizontal containers match the tallest element in their row, and vertically aligned [`st.columns`](/develop/api-reference/layout/st.columns) fill the row height ([#17392](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17392)).
- 🦠 Bug fix: Stretch-height charts fall back to their default height when nothing gives them one, and stretch-height containers and forms grow to fit their content ([#17410](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17410), [#17424](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17424)).
- 🦟 Bug fix: [`st.echarts_chart`](/develop/api-reference/charts/st.echarts_chart) tooltips use the theme's font weight and round long numbers ([#17333](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17333)).
- 🦂 Bug fix: [`st.pydeck_chart`](/develop/api-reference/charts/st.pydeck_chart) tooltips appear at the cursor instead of above it ([#17313](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17313), [#17309](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17309)).
- 🦗 Bug fix: Buttons, checkboxes, toggles, and other labels show a hover tooltip only when their text is cut off ([#17266](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17266), [#17264](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17264)).

- 🐌 Bug fix: Screen readers skip Material icons and decorative images, and icon-only controls have accessible names ([#17170](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17170), [#12873](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12873)).
- 🦎 Bug fix: The sidebar's expand and collapse buttons report their state with `aria-expanded`. Custom CSS or scripts that read `aria-expanded` on the sidebar should use `data-collapsed` instead ([#17293](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17293)).
